title: Wind Tunnel Based System Identification of a Small Unmanned Aircraft System
relevance: Physical static and dynamic tunnel campaigns identify aerodynamic derivatives and pitch damping for a modified SIG Kadet LT-40 called Urban Condor. The 2 m, flapped wing and research fixture are described; a six-component balance and Pixhawk 6X pitch-rate measurement support a linear short-period model across airspeeds.
limitations: This is a research-modified Kadet tested on a rig, not the stock trainer in free flight. The model is longitudinal/short-period, and the paper does not release raw measurements. Its coefficients depend on the test rig, configuration and reference geometry.
license: No separate open-reuse license stated in the retained copy
read_depth: Full ten-page paper inspected; test article, wind-tunnel methods, parameters and operating limits checked

title: In-situ Calibration of Four-Hole Pressure Probes on a Small UAV for Free Flight Measurement
relevance: Calibrates cone-shaped four-hole probes alone and installed on a modified SIG Kadet LT-40 Urban Condor in the wind tunnel. The paper details how the airframe flow, control deflections, angular motion and tunnel blockage affect pressure-probe estimates, useful when assessing low-cost AoA/sideslip sensing.
limitations: The main result is probe calibration, not whole-aircraft aerodynamic coefficients or a flight system-identification model. It provides no public flight log; separate pilot flights are mentioned only as handling context. The calibration is specific to the probe installation and tested envelope.
license: No separate open-reuse license stated in the retained copy
read_depth: Full paper inspected; airframe identity, probe installation, calibration procedures and tunnel corrections checked

title: Flight Test Based System Identification of an Unmanned Fixed-Wing Aircraft
relevance: Full paper reports 15 actual flights of Urban Condor X, a 2 m-span modified SIG Kadet LT-40 with modular 3D-printed wing, at about 7.6 kg flight mass. Pixhawk 6X measurements at 200 Hz support elevator chirp/3211 short-period excitation, phugoid pulses and gliding drag tests at multiple airspeeds.
limitations: Longitudinal-only identification; initial aerodynamic estimates use vortex-lattice calculations. No raw flight logs are published. This flight campaign is distinct from the related Urban Condor wind-tunnel campaigns. The official PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 to direct download; no access challenge was bypassed.
read_depth: Full text inspected online; no local original (HTTP 403)

title: Real-Time System Identification of a Small Multi-Engine Aircraft
relevance: Reports real flight-test system identification on Georgia Tech's instrumented Multiplex TwinStar II, a 4.7 ft-span foam twin. Closed-loop sum-of-sines inputs and onboard air-data, angular-rate and attitude estimates support recursive frequency-domain estimation of a complete linear 6-DOF model.
limitations: Research-instrumented and modified airframe, with thrust inferred from a ground-developed model rather than measured in flight. The paper reports methods and selected plots, not public raw logs. A related damaged-wing follow-up and a later model-identification paper use the GT TwinStar platform and may overlap the same broader test program.
license: AIAA copyright; no open-reuse license stated
read_depth: Full paper text inspected; aircraft identity, instrumentation, experiment design and model validation reviewed

title: Modeling and Scaling of a Flexible Subscale Aircraft for Flight Control Development and Testing in the Presence of Aeroservoelastic Interactions
relevance: Virginia Tech dissertation documents a subscale Rascal-based flexible aircraft, configuration and scaling work, with physical flight tests and aeroservoelastic interaction analysis. Chapters on the Rascal-derived test articles provide unusually detailed mass/inertia and structural context for a named conventional RC platform.
limitations: The research airframe is substantially modified for flexibility and instrumentation; its elastic structure and aeroelastic purpose make its response unlike a stock SIG Rascal. Simulation also uses aerodynamic lookup/VLM methods. Use physical parameters only for the described configuration, not as stock-Rascal coefficients.
license: Not stated; public institutional thesis, redistribution not inferred
read_depth: Full thesis text inspected; Rascal test-article, scaling, inertial and flight-test chapters reviewed

title: Advanced Modeling of UAV Dynamics Using Artificial Neural Networks and the Output Error Method
relevance: Uses designed flight-test data from a Multiplex FunCub R/C with multistep elevator input to estimate longitudinal dynamics using output-error/maximum-likelihood and neural-network methods. The paper reports a 1.96 kg aircraft, pitch inertia of 0.095 kg m² and cruise near 21 m/s.
limitations: Only longitudinal dynamics are identified. Actual test data are mixed with simulated noise/drift augmentation; reported mass/inertia are not accompanied by a repeatable measurement procedure. No raw logs are released. Results are configuration-specific and should not be treated as a full 6-DOF model.
read_depth: Full article inspected; identified model, flight-versus-simulation data distinction and reported parameters checked

title: System Identification and Parameter Space Control Design for a Small Unmanned Aircraft
relevance: DLR thesis identifies the longitudinal model of the named Penguin BE using output-error and two-step methods on actual flight-test data. The DLR record says the thesis is 57 pages and describes the aircraft's cooperative landing research role.
limitations: A single-axis model for one test configuration, not a complete 6-DOF database. No raw flight logs are released. This study and Lee's companion 2017 thesis draw on the DLR Penguin BE program and should not be counted as independent aircraft/campaign evidence without checking maneuver overlap.
license: DLR repository open access; no separate reuse license stated
read_depth: Full thesis searchable text inspected; Penguin BE setup, selected flight data, identification and validation chapters reviewed

title: High Fidelity Modelling for High Altitude Long Endurance Solar Powered Aircraft
relevance: DLR's master thesis describes multiple actual flight-test system-identification experiments, validation data and aerodynamic derivative estimation. Chapter 3 includes the Penguin BE; the wider thesis also addresses the Elektra One Solar platform and methods intended to transfer across fixed-wing types.
limitations: The work spans multiple airframes and identification methods; do not attribute every reported parameter to Penguin BE. Penguin coverage is longitudinal and shares the DLR research program with Coelho (2017). Raw flight recordings are not released with the thesis.
license: DLR repository open access; no separate reuse license stated
read_depth: Full thesis searchable text inspected; test campaigns, validation, aircraft-specific chapters and parameter limits reviewed

title: sUAS Position Estimation and Fusion in GPS-Degraded and GPS-Denied Environments using an ADS-B Transponder and Local Area Multilateration
relevance: University of Washington thesis documents actual Skywalker 1900 flight demonstrations for ADS-B and local-area multilateration position-estimation systems. It identifies the test airframe as 'Leia' and reports configuration dimensions and mass useful for platform identity.
limitations: This is navigation/sensor demonstration evidence, not aerodynamic identification or flight-dynamics validation. The thesis does not provide an open raw telemetry dataset or a validated coefficient model; student/test installation details constrain transfer.
license: Not stated; publicly accessible institutional thesis, redistribution not inferred
read_depth: Full thesis searchable text inspected; Skywalker configuration and flight-demonstration sections reviewed

title: Synthesis and Flight Test of Automatic Landing Controller Using Quantitative Feedback Theory
relevance: Reports actual automatic-landing tests using a modified Multiplex EasyStar II and compares measured landing time histories with simulation. The paper highlights model uncertainty and flight-controller redesign needs under practical wind and sensor limitations.
limitations: The evidence is two closed-loop automatic landings, not open-loop aerodynamic system identification; simulation and Monte Carlo analyses are distinct from measured results. The vehicle is modified and no raw flight logs are published.
license: AIAA copyright; no open-reuse license stated
read_depth: Full paper inspected; EasyStar configuration, simulation/flight-test separation and two landing results checked

title: Development of Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Platform: Modeling, Simulating, and Flight Testing
relevance: AFIT thesis metadata and abstract describe physical, inertial and aerodynamic modeling of a SIG Rascal 110 plus open-loop and autonomous flight tests with post-flight comparison against a nonlinear 6-DOF simulation. The reported physical configuration and mass/inertia work make it a strong model-identity lead.
limitations: Full thesis PDF was not obtainable from AFIT or DTIC endpoints during this pass (HTTP 403). The abstract says Digital DATCOM contributed to aerodynamic modeling; it does not establish measured aerodynamic coefficients. This manifest record is metadata/abstract-level, not a full-text audit.
license: AFIT item describes public-release material; PDF reuse terms not verified
read_depth: AFIT institutional metadata and abstract inspected; full text unavailable locally

limitations: The journal/conference full PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403; this is an abstract-level record. The aircraft is a research-modified TwinStar and likely part of the same broader GT flight-test program as other TwinStar papers. No raw flight logs located.

title: Aerodynamic System Identification of Fixed-wing UAV
relevance: The paper identifies its platform as a Multiplex TwinStar II/GT TwinStar and fits an LTI model with output-error methods against real flight measurements; its reported poor fits and unstable identified modes are useful examples of the limits of basic linearization and data preparation.
limitations: Publisher PDF returned HTTP 403; this entry uses a primary bibliographic record and abstract, cross-checked against a full-text author copy during discovery. It appears to reuse the GT TwinStar program and may overlap with the 2009 paper; not an independent model aircraft dataset. No raw logs found.
license: AIAA copyright; no open-reuse license stated
read_depth: Primary metadata/abstract inspected; full-text author copy was cross-checked for aircraft identity and fit limitations, but no local original retained

title: Determination of Power Required through Accelerated Flight with Application to Unmanned Vehicles
relevance: The thesis reports real acceleration/deceleration runs using a Hobbico NexStar and an NCSU Raspberry Pi logger to estimate power-required behavior, with comparison against the classical PIW-VIW method. It specifically discusses poorer acceleration-run quality due to engine/propeller vibration noise.
limitations: Performance/power estimation, not a full aerodynamic or flight-dynamics model; many data points are excluded for assumption violations. Direct retrieval returned an 8,937-byte Anubis challenge page, not the thesis. No challenge page was bypassed and no local file was retained.
access: repository item indexed; download blocked by Anubis challenge HTML
license: Not verified; institutional thesis metadata available
read_depth: Thesis text indexed by the institutional repository and search; aircraft, test method and limitations inspected in indexed passages; original not locally available

title: CAMEX-4 Aerosonde V1
relevance: NASA GHRC's mission dataset contains measurements from real Aerosonde aircraft flights during CAMEX-4 (19 August–10 September 2001), with downloadable per-flight spreadsheet granules including airborne meteorological observations. It is a primary real-flight data route for an identified small fixed-wing UAS.
limitations: The representative granule redirects to Earthdata authentication (HTTP 401); access requires an Earthdata account. The listed product is meteorological, not a control-surface/IMU system-identification log, so it does not provide an aerodynamic model. No data were mirrored.
access: NASA CMR metadata public; granules require Earthdata authentication (HTTP 401)
license: U.S. Government work; see https://www.usa.gov/government-works and NASA dataset terms
read_depth: NASA CMR collection metadata and granule listing inspected; a representative granule URL was tested but requires Earthdata login
